newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma wheat harvest advances in hot weather.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma wheat harvest advances in hot weather.

text.p: Harvesting of Oklahoma's wheat crop advanced during the week ended Sunday thanks to mostly hot, dry weather, the state's agricultural statistics service said Monday in its crop progress report.
Statewide, harvest was 91 percent complete, lagging 100 percent last year and 92 percent for the five-year average.

"Harvest ranged from 63 percent complete in the Northeast district to 98 percent in the Southwest district. Test weights in some localities dropped below 60 pounds on wheat cut after rain delays. Stubble has been plowed at least once on 41 percent of the state's acreage," the report said.

Corn was rated 86 percent in good to excellent condition, below 91 percent in that category a week ago. Sixty percent of the state's corn was tasseling, against 77 percent last week and 50 percent on average.
Sorghum was rated 74 percent in good to excellent condition, against 87 percent at that level last week. Sorghum was 93 percent planted, behind 99 last year and 94 on average.
Soybeans were rated 63 percent good to excellent, unchanged from a week earlier. Topsoil moisture was rated nil very short, 13 percent short, 85 percent adequate and two percent surplus.
